With COMMITTEE set, an order whose envelope is not a curve point gets no partials, so the committee wait would hold the auction until abandon; fixed with partialable() and an e2e test

The 2-of-3 Safe's three signer keys were generated together and are kept on one machine, so one compromise of it yields a quorum; bounded by the 48 h timelock, alerts on every queued call and exits no owner power can block (SECURITY.md risk 3)

Depositor screening depends on Chainalysis's sanctions API (no on-chain oracle on 4663); fail-closed for new depositors; an API error keeps the last verdict and a removed label still proves against the gate's last eight roots until replaced (SECURITY.md risk 4)

A committee member computed partials for any ciphertext the operator listed (6321eeb checked only that it rests in a pinned auction, which a copy placed in an earlier-pinning auction passes: the independent check traced it). Each order envelope now carries a Schnorr proof of its ciphertext's ephemeral key bound to chain, pool, auction and commitment (src/shielded/committee.ts proveEphemeral); members and the operator serve or wait for an order only when it verifies, which also closes the relay front-run variant (operator-relayer copying a relayed ciphertext into an earlier-pinning auction) and related keys (−R, k·R). e2e plants the copy and checks the original still opens; committee.check.ts covers related keys and every binding

Under the unique-key rule (2c65419), copying a resting order's ciphertext made members refuse the original too (griefing; the independent check rated it Medium: any screened depositor, normal state). The key proof replaced that rule: a copy fails its own proof and the original is served as usual (e2e: the victim's order opens after the copy is refused)
